newsitem.title: USA: PointCast still on track for IPO this year-CEO.
newsitem.headline: PointCast still on track for IPO this year-CEO.

text.p: PointCast Inc, the pioneer of Internet direct broadcasting technology, said it remains on track to go public sometime this year and denied recent rumors that it is in talks to be acquired.

"Our intent is not to remain private," said PointCast CEO Christopher Hassett. "An IPO is definitely a possibility in the near future." While Hassett declined to give any specific time frame for a possible initial public offering, he said this spring and summer are "reasonable timeframes."
He denied recent rumors swirling in the industry that the company was in talks to be acquired by News Corp Ltd.
"That's a rumor. There are no facts behind that," he said, adding that PointCast is always in talks with media companies, because many are partners in providing news to the PointCast Network.

PointCast, based in Cupertino, Calif., developed the concept of "push" technology and has a network that delivers news and other content directly to a subscriber's desktop PC instead of users having to go to different Web sites and look for and receive news, stock quotes, sports scores, etc.
It has many media giants as its content providers and partners, from Times Mirror Co, the New York Times Co, Reuters Holdings Plc and others.
Last week, rumors were swirling that News Corp, the media giant that owns Fox News, TV Guide, The New York Post and 20th Century Fox, was going to acquire PointCast for $300 million to $400 million.
"I can tell you flat out that there is zero percent chance of that, that's just not going to happen," Hassett said. "It's just not factual."
He also said merging with Microsoft Corp, another less-discussed rumor, is not a possibility.
"Microsoft is a partner of ours, we are not in acquisition discussions with Microsoft," Hassett said.
He said that PointCast has an investment banker, Morgan Stanley, whom it has worked with for private placement deals and other banking transactions.
"They would do our IPO," Hassett said. He declined to provide any financial details on the company.
